notes: The player and {name} never take a gendered past-tense verb or adjective (postavil/postavila, připraven/připravena): present tense, imperative, impersonal forms or nouns instead.
Placeholders always stand in the nominative, after a colon or in apposition (Vylepšit: {building}, budova {building}); no case endings or prepositions that need a case are attached to them.
Plurals use all four Czech categories: one, few (2-4), many (fractions) and other (0, 5+).

Generated names are noun-first with a space (generatedNames: noun-first): second parts are nominative nouns (Vrchol, Průsmyk, Údolí), first parts genitive nouns that fit any gender (Hromu, Mlh, Železa): Průsmyk Hromu, Údolí Železa.

Czech letters (č ř š ž ě ů) are outside the bundled Latin-1 fonts, so Czech needs SYSTEM_FONT_LANGS and the styles.css lang rule (integration step; tests/locales/latin-fonts.test.ts fails for cs until then).
The Japanese statutory pages are translated into Czech; the support page links them with their Japanese titles.
Computer players’ generated names (Kaito Mori) are stored text and stay in Latin letters, as in every language.
